newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAA in 45 mln rand IT network upgrade.
newsitem.headline: SAA in 45 mln rand IT network upgrade.

text.p: South African Airways (SAA) said on Wednesday it would spend about 45 million rand to upgrade its reservations and information delivery networks over the next three years.

It said the upgrade was one of the largest in the country's information technology (IT) industry and would accommodate over 16,000 terminal devices at over 1,000 remote sites, including high-speed connectivity to the United States and Europe.

"This whole contract is there to upgrade our existing reservations system so that we can have more reservations sites available and to help further the services of SAA," SAA spokesman Leon Els told Reuters.
"This will also give us the international link," he added.
Els said the company had awarded its networking contract to Transtel, a unit of the state's transporation parastatal, Transnet, and two overseas companies, Centera and Zervos.

It said Transtel would focus on data delivery, while Centera would look at the networks's functionality which should facilitate electronic mail, faxing, inter-branch connectivity and the provision of the global internet service.

Els said present-form network link-ups of South Africa and other world travel agencies operating with SAA did not make it possible for tourists to have a broad range of services, such as booking accommodation, car and airline tickets all at once.
"This (upgrade) is an added service availability for the public. It will give us added advantages of doing normal reservations and other reservations as well," he said.
